summary: Parameterized SLA templates causing routing window misapplication for internal queues
description:
Issue summary:
A recent deploy of parameterized SLA templates to the support-rule-engine resulted in routing windows (time-based priority overrides) being applied to the wrong internal queues. The misapplied windows caused internal support queues to deprioritize incoming P1 tickets for ~45 minutes across two regions.

Impact:
- Internal support ticket routing in prod (us-east-1, eu-west-1) dropped priority for ~45 minutes on 2026-03-01 between 14:20-15:05 UTC.
- Resulted in missed SLO alerts and delayed handoff for critical infrastructure incidents.
- No customer-facing outages reported but internal SLA adherence metrics were affected and on-call load increased.

Background:
- We introduced parameterized SLA templates in the rule-engine (PR #1427) to allow per-team SLA overrides using the new expression language (tmpl_v2). The templates allow windows and tenant variables to be injected at rollout-time.
- A data-mapping bug in the rollout orchestration mapped tenant_id -> team_name in the routing rule context resulting in windows keyed by team_name instead of tenant_id.

Steps to reproduce (dev environment):
1. Checkout release branch: git checkout release/support-tmpl-v2
2. Apply template set: POST /internal/sla/templates with body template-set-v2.json (see attached sample in related_confluence_pages).
3. Create two internal queues: "infra-ops" (team_name: infra, tenant_id: t-003) and "platform-sre" (team_name: platform, tenant_id: t-008).
4. Create a parameterized window: window({team: '{{team_name}}', start: '14:00', end: '15:00', priority: 'low'})
5. Send a high-priority ticket destined for infra-ops during the window.
6. Observe rule-engine apply: routing decision shows window keyed to team_name across both queues.

Observed behavior:
- Window applied to both infra-ops and platform-sre regardless of tenant_id.
- Metrics: support-routing-delay increased by ~220% for internal P1 tickets during the window.
- Rule-engine logs show context.payload contains {"team_name": "infra","tenant_id": "t-003"} but matching lookup used team_name for tenant_index lookup.

Expected behavior:
- Windows should be keyed and applied by tenant_id for multi-tenant isolation. The template parameterization should respect explicit tenant_id when provided.

Logs / evidence:
- Routing trace: routing-trace-20260301-1425 (attached link to S3 trace).
- Rule-engine log excerpt: "match_key resolved to 'infra' for tenant_lookup, lookup returned global-window-14"
- Dashboard: support-console/slo/internal-slo-ops shows spike in time-to-first-response between 14:20-15:05 UTC.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Rolled back rollout orchestration to tmpl_v1 for both regions at 15:10 UTC (rollback PR #1436).
- Re-enabled explicit tenant scoping in a hotfix to the runtime mapping layer (PR #1437), staged to prod at 15:25 UTC.
- Temporarily disabled parameterized windows until full validation added.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: rollout orchestration introduced mapping inversion when building match_key for windows. Verified by adding a unit test that failed in release branch.
- Hypothesis B: rule-engine's runtime context resolution prefers team_name when both team_name and tenant_id are present; root cause found in runtime key resolution table.
- Early root cause: mapping function build_context_keys(context) returned keys in priority order [team_name, tenant_id] instead of [tenant_id, team_name] because of a missing explicit sort in the template resolver.

Next steps / Action items:
- Patch: enforce ordering in build_context_keys to prefer tenant_id, add explicit schema validation for templates (assigned PR #1440).
- Add regression test: integration test that creates multi-tenant queues and validates window application by tenant_id. (owner: Marco Li, due: 2026-03-07).
- Add alert rule: routing-window-seen-on-multiple-tenants (PagerDuty) to catch cross-tenant window application quickly.
- Postmortem: schedule postmortem doc in Confluence and runbook updates for template rollouts.

Workaround (until fix is in place):
- Use non-parameterized static SLA templates for multi-tenant internal queues.
- Manually validate mapping output using staging harness before rollout.

Attachments / Links:
- routing-trace-20260301-1425: s3://redwood-support/traces/routing-trace-20260301-1425.json
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1436
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1437
- Template design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPP/Parameterized+SLA+Templates
comments: 2026-03-01 15:12 - Marco Li: Rolled back tmpl_v2 rollout in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Observed time-to-first-response returning to baseline after rollback.
2026-03-01 16:05 - Devon Chen: Added temporary rule to reject templates that contain ambiguous keys without explicit tenant_id. Deploying to staging for verification. See PR #1437.
2026-03-03 09:22 - Aisha Patel: Post-deploy verification checklist created. Integration test outline added to the repo. Assigned Marco for test implementation.
2026-03-04 13:47 - SRE On-call (Jorge Ramos): Noted one retry loop in rule-engine during hotfix rollout at 15:23 UTC but did not impact request latencies beyond the event window.
2026-03-05 11:08 - Marco Li: Patch PR #1440 created to enforce key ordering and added schema validation. Requesting review from @dev-tools and @rule-engine team.
investigation_notes: Unit test failure correlated with template resolver change in release/support-tmpl-v2 branch.
build_context_keys ordering bug reproduced in a minimal harness; switching order resolves incorrect match behavior.
No indication of data corruption; issue is deterministic given the existing templates and context payload structure.
resolution: In progress: hotfix applied and rollback performed; awaiting code review and CI for full fix (PR #1440). Regression tests to be merged before closing the ticket.
additional_notes: Recommend adding a preflight validator for template rollouts that runs the template against a sampled set of tenant contexts to detect cross-tenant match keys before deployment.
